title: Tz-L-M
hook: tzelem, image, as in the image of God

segments.voice: Yesterday, K-B-D: kaved, heavy, and kavod, honor, Moses' tired hands held up on the hill. Your line was honor is weight. Whose words did you let land? Today, a root about faces. Day one thousand three hundred eighty-five.

Rush hour. A train car packed shoulder to shoulder. A man asleep against the window with his mouth open. A teenager with headphones and a scowl. A woman doing her makeup in her phone's camera. Someone who smells like the gym, someone humming, someone crying quietly behind sunglasses. Nobody looks at anybody. Now read the first chapter of Genesis, and it makes a claim about every one of those faces. A big claim, in a short word. Three letters, tzadi, lamed, mem: Tz-L-M. Tzelem. Image.
screen: `A PACKED TRAIN CAR.` → `NOBODY LOOKS AT ANYBODY.` → `TZ-L-M: IMAGE.`

segments.voice: Turn tzelem four ways. First, the verse: "And God created man in His own image, in the image of God created He him; male and female created He them." Tzelem, twice. And then a third line, so nobody misses who's included: male and female. Second, what the word names elsewhere. In other books of the Bible, tzelem can mean a statue, a carved figure, like the images of Baal that the people of the land break in pieces in the book of Kings. A tzelem is something that stands for someone. So Genesis takes a word for a figure carved in stone and uses it for a person made of dust and breath. Third, the coins. The Mishnah, in tractate Sanhedrin, says it like this: a human king stamps many coins with one seal, and they all come out alike. God stamped every person with the seal of the first human, and not one of them is like another. One image, and endless faces. Fourth, what follows. After the flood, God tells Noah that whoever sheds a person's blood will answer for it, "for in the image of God made He man." Harm a person, and you've struck at the image. Rabbi Akiva, in Pirkei Avot, adds a softer line: a human is beloved, created in the image, and more beloved still that it was made known to him. Go back to the train car. The sleeper. The scowler. The one crying behind sunglasses. Genesis doesn't say they're nice, or right, or easy to sit next to. It says each of them carries the image.
screen: `IN THE IMAGE OF GOD CREATED HE HIM.` · `A TZELEM: A FIGURE THAT STANDS FOR.` · `ONE SEAL, AND NO TWO ALIKE.` · `HARM A PERSON, STRIKE THE IMAGE.` · then, large: `צֶלֶם`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: see the image in someone. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind a face you passed recently without really seeing it. A stranger in a line, a driver, someone you find hard. Hold the face for a moment. Notice something particular about it, something no other face has: a crease, a habit, the way they stand. One seal, and no two alike. Stay with that face for a few breaths. If you pray, you can hold that person in the quiet. The bell holds the time.
Tz-L-M. Tzadi, lamed, mem: tzelem, image, the word Genesis uses for every human being made in the image of God. Today's word.
Your line: the image. Today, when someone irritates you, look at their face one second longer, and notice one thing about it that's only theirs. Day one thousand three hundred eighty-five.

howItsDone: Jewish teaching draws on tzelem Elohim, the image of God in every person, when it speaks about human dignity; the Mishnah's teaching about one seal and no two faces alike is studied as part of tractate Sanhedrin.

myth: Genesis says only the man was made in God's image
the verse adds: "male and female created He them."
elsewhere in the Bible, tzelem can mean a statue
the book of Kings uses it for the images of Baal.
in the Mishnah, everyone stamped with God's seal comes out the same
a king's coins come out alike; God's seal makes no two people alike.

fork.setup: a king stamps many coins with one seal, and they all come out alike. God stamps every person with one seal. what comes out?
options: people who are all the same.
people who are each unlike any other.
fork.reveal: the Mishnah says not one is like another. one image, endless faces.

original.note: Hebrew: image; as in tzelem Elohim, the image of God.

trapdoor: what you thought: the image of God means people look like God.
what it means: tzelem is a figure that stands for someone, and Genesis gives that word to every human.
what a scholar hears: Mishnah Sanhedrin's coins: a king's seal makes copies; God's seal makes no two alike.

notes: Editor: Avot 3:14 says the image 'was made known to him', not 'to us'; fixed; dropped 'usually' (a frequency claim) from the tzelem-as-statue step.
Confirm JPS 1917 wording of Genesis 1:27 and the closing clause of Genesis 9:6.
2 Kings 11:18 (tzelamav, the images of Baal broken down) paraphrased; confirm the Hebrew uses tzelem there.
Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5 paraphrased (coins from one seal; first human; none like another). Confirm.
Avot 3:14 (Rabbi Akiva; numbered 3:18 in some editions) paraphrased. Confirm numbering.
